Here's my setup: Windows 8 installed on a 120GB main drive, with all of my media on two matching 6TB drives, both formatted as NTFS. I would really like to replace Windows 8 with Fedora Linux because literally all I use this computer for is to run Plex, MakeMKV, and Handbrake. I don't see a big future with Windows on this PC and I like how lightweight Fedora is by comparison.
My problem is that I've installed Fedora and installed Plex, but I can't for the life of me get Plex to see my 6TB NTFS content hard drives. Doing some research it looks like Linux doesn't play well with NTFS and can't translate user permissions to the NTFS drive, which is why I can see my movies in nautilus file explorer but Plex can't see the drive. Does anyone have experience with this issue and might be able to shed some light on my problem? Thank you very much for your time!

Resolution: it turns out Fedora already gives me the tools I need to mount and access NTFS drives; the problem was my mount point. The default mount point was /run/media/kyle, which didn't work because the user "plex" that the server uses doesn't have access to that folder. I used Fedora's built-in "disks" program to move the mount point to /mnt/plexstorage and the service saw it immediately and I was able to add the folders to my library. Thank you so much for your help and for pointing me in the right direction. I can definitely say my experience with this sub has been a great one. Thank for helping me fix my Linux!

The problem is that the NTFS partition of your bigger drives is a proprietary format that Windows uses to store files over 4Gb in size, which is something FAT32 cannot do. So you are looking in the right direction, you need a package to help Fedora read from and write to NTFS. Installing ntfs-3g or one that has fuse in the name (I can't remember the name at the moment) should do the trick. I don't think you'll need to reboot after the install but that's a hit and miss pattern. My first suggestion would be to remount those drives.

Afterward, you can either edit your fstab file directly or use a GUI tool like gnome-disk-utility to set it to auto mount on boot.

If your like to PM me any questions, feel free. I use Fedora 22 as my daily OS with handbrake on it and I run a Plex server. So I do have experience with what you're trying to set up.

I got it figured out! The problem was the mount point. The default mount point at /run/media/kyle was throwing off my permissions because it didn't want to give the "plex" user permissions to my "kyle" folder. I changed the mount point to /mnt/plexstorage and plex saw it immediately. Thank you for your help, especially the tip on the gnome disk utility!
